script.base: Spread and total were not saved, so this is form-only, not the book's expected leader. Base case is a competitive game: JAX leans on B.Tuten (43 carries, 204 yards) into a CIN run defense allowing 5.00 YPC, while T.Lawrence mostly sees a clean pocket (CIN blitz 14%; his EPA/dropback is +0.45 unblitzed vs -0.23 on 25 blitzed dropbacks) and feeds P.Washington (23 targets, 329 air yards). CIN can throw via J.Chase (25 targets, 185 yards) and T.Higgins (23 targets, 244 yards, 302 air), but J.Burrow is -0.31 EPA on 36 blitzed dropbacks and JAX blitzes 32%, so CIN pass downs tilt shorter toward M.Gesicki; C.Brown (49/197) faces a tighter JAX run defense (3.79 YPC).
script.flip1: JAX falls behind and abandons the run: Tuten's carries die, Washington/J.Meyers/B.Strange targets spike, and Brown bleeds the clock while Chase/Higgins volume stalls.
script.flip2: The JAX blitz never shows or both QBs stay clean in a shootout: Higgins (302 air yards) and Washington (329 air yards) clear on explosives together, and a clock-killing rush stack loses.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location only: CIN allows 9.23 YPA middle (30 att), 8.43 left (37), 5.67 right (48) — middle and left bleed, right is the strength. JAX allows 14.45 YPA middle on only 11 att, 8.66 left (38), 7.14 right (35).
matchup.pressure: CIN blitz 14% is a clean pocket for Lawrence (+0.45 EPA unblitzed vs -0.23 on 25 blitzed dropbacks). JAX blitz 32% is the problem look for Burrow (-0.31 EPA on 36 blitzed dropbacks vs +0.32 unblitzed). Pressure that gets home should cut CIN deep-WR efficiency and lift TE/RB checkdowns.
matchup.bleeds: CIN run defense allows 5.00 YPC and 8 runs of 10+, plus 12 passes of 20+ on 125 attempts. JAX run defense allows 3.79 YPC and only 5 runs of 10+, but 13 passes of 20+ on 92 attempts (higher explosive rate). No YAC or stuff-rate charting saved.
matchup.overlap: Core overlap is Tuten's share (43 of 73 JAX RB carries) into CIN's 5.00 YPC run defense. Second is Gesicki (10 targets, 95 air yards — he releases, he is not a pure blocker) into JAX's 32% blitz, the environment where Burrow's EPA collapses and throws shorten. Washington's 329 air yards vs CIN's middle/left bleed and 14% blitz is a real overlap, but 221 yards sit just under 76.5 so it is not a bet. Chase/Higgins into JAX's explosive rate is offset by the blitz.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Tuten is the lead back at 43 carries and 204 yards (68 a game) and CIN has allowed 5.00 YPC with 8 runs of 10+, so even a trimmed 12-carry day at that rate clears 57.5.
edge_players.must_be_true: Tuten keeps the early-down share (about 14 carries, not a Rodriguez/Abdullah takeover), Lawrence plays so the offense stays on schedule, and JAX is not in a multi-score hole by halftime.
edge_players.kills_it: JAX trails big and abandons the run, a late scratch or snap limit not in this pack, or CIN's 5.00 YPC is a soft-schedule mirage and they hold him under 4.0.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Gesicki has averaged 38.3 receiving yards on 10 targets and 95 air yards, and JAX's 32% blitz is the look that drops Burrow to -0.31 EPA and shortens throws to a TE who already releases, so 27.5 is under the role.
edge_players.must_be_true: Gesicki releases instead of staying in to block the blitz, Burrow plays, and CIN has enough dropbacks for about 3+ targets.
edge_players.kills_it: Max-protect keeps him chipping, Sample or Perine steal the short area, or CIN leads and runs Brown so the TE volume never shows; the 115 yards could also be one explosive we cannot split out.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost. Tuten went about 11-41 because JAX was down two scores by the half, Rodriguez (already 20 carries in three games) took the hurry-up work, and CIN's 5.00 YPC was three soft opponents rather than a structural hole — opponent logs are not in the pack. Gesicki finished 1-9 because the blitz plan was max protect and he chipped instead of releasing, and the 115 yards were a single explosive buried in the three-game total. Missing spread is the hole in the Tuten leg; missing game logs are the hole in the Gesicki leg.
slip_story: One competitive-game story: JAX runs on a soft CIN front (Tuten rush over) while CIN dropbacks are stressed by a 32% blitz and tilt to the releasing TE (Gesicki rec over). Do not add Chase or Higgins overs (those need the blitz to fail) or a total (not saved, and this stack needs dropbacks). No TDs, one market per player. If JAX trails big, Tuten dies — that is why this is not a 4-leg slip.
